title: Store agent: policy, invented facts, choice

headlines.label: Store-agent replies offered or auto-sent outside the store policy
headlines.baseline: model picks any reply: 30 of 100 not allowed
headlines.note: Invariant checks over 20 cases and 70 offered replies (50 inside the policy, so sent without staff): declined replies, part-refund percent and amount, the staff limit, auto-send rules.

headlines.label: Invented facts in store-agent reasons that reach the buyer
headlines.note: Scripted model answers on hand-labelled cases; run --live for a real model. One invented amount, size, colour, date, number, percentage or quote per answer, a reason citing no fact or a fact that does not exist, a reason describing a reply that was not chosen, or "refund" where nothing is refunded.

headlines.label: Grounded store-agent reasons kept by the check
headlines.note: Scripted model answers on hand-labelled cases; run --live for a real model. Reasons that restate the case's facts, some reworded.

headlines.label: Model picks of a reply the policy does not allow that get sent
headlines.note: Scripted model answers on hand-labelled cases; run --live for a real model. Includes replies the buyer already declined and part refunds the policy does not allow.

headlines.label: Rule-based fallback (no model) picks a reply a fair store would
headlines.note: Labels written by hand before any model ran, by the author of the code.

headlines.label: Vague claims with no checkable detail that reach the buyer as unattributed statements
headlines.note: Scripted model answers on hand-labelled cases; run --live for a real model. "This sweater is a favourite with returning customers." and "Demo Store always replaces items within a day." on each case, next to a grounded reason: 20 reached the buyer only as "The store says: …", 20 were dropped (promises with no fact behind them).

headlines.label: More vague claims and promises that reach the buyer as unattributed statements
headlines.note: Scripted model answers on hand-labelled cases; run --live for a real model. Ten more phrasings (praise, reassurance, superlatives, "we guarantee", "never", "definitely") written before the check: 120 attributed, 80 dropped.

headlines.label: Fact-backed reasons the vague-claim check drops or rewrites
headlines.note: Scripted model answers on hand-labelled cases; run --live for a real model. Every fact a reason may use for the chosen reply, word for word, plus reworded check and shipping facts, each as the only reason. 219 kept as written; 0 kept out by older rules (a fact that says "you" is not read to the buyer).

limitations: Model answers are scripted; the suite does not call a model. `pnpm --filter @sightline/evals store-agent -- --live` sends a few cases to the fast model and prints what it picked, without writing results.
The 20 cases and their "fair reply" labels were written by the author of the code, and so were the vague claims (evals/store-agent/vague.ts, committed before the vague-claim check).

The invented-fact check is token-level: amounts, sizes, colours, dates, numbers, percentages and quotes. A reason with none of those must share most of its words with the facts it cites; otherwise it is read only as "The store says: …", and a promise word ("always", "never", "guarantee", "definitely") that no cited fact uses drops it. A false claim worded with the facts' own words still passes.

"Before" is the previous run (evals/results/store-agent.json written by evals/store-agent/run.ts at commit 73ce251, 2026-11-09T13:26:41.663Z), when vague claims were measured as the only reason in an answer.
